answer: Behavioral tide clustering. Each identity accrues a timing kernel of inter-action intervals; agents whose kernels correlate above threshold across many low-value actions get merged into one cluster retroactively. A rising tide of shared burst windows flags coordinated batches. Clusters pay one fee per detected member, priced in quartz-equivalent compute credits. Honest agents acting alone stay below correlation bounds; a sybil farm must stagger behavior across independent schedules, raising per-identity setup cost.
